title: Attention Mechanism in Transformer Neural Networks
key_points: Attention uses Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V) matrices to compute weighted relationships between all positions in a sequence simultaneously, enabling parallel processing.
Multi-head attention applies multiple attention heads with different learned projections to capture diverse types of relationships and dependencies across the sequence.
Scaled dot-product attention computes attention weights as softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)), where scaling by the square root of key dimension stabilizes gradient flow during training.
Self-attention allows each token to attend to all other tokens in the sequence, eliminating the recurrence limitations of RNNs and enabling better long-range dependency modeling.
Positional encoding adds information about token positions to embeddings, since attention itself is position-agnostic and needs explicit position context.
limitations: This summary focuses on the core mathematical and architectural components but does not extensively cover implementation details (e.g., dropout, normalization), computational complexity analysis (O(n²) scaling), practical applications across different domains, or recent variants and improvements to standard attention (such as sparse attention, linear attention, or other optimizations). The explanation also simplifies some mathematical notation for clarity.
